title: Closing active tab shows wrong conversation (no navigation, jumps to last tab); Ctrl+Z cannot undo a paste in the composer
evidence: TAB CLOSE: src/renderer/pages/conversation/components/ConversationTabs.tsx:179-190 handleCloseTab calls closeTab(tabId) and only navigates when NO tabs remain; its comment 'context auto-handles navigation' is false — ConversationTabsContext.tsx closeTab (src/renderer/pages/conversation/hooks/ConversationTabsContext.tsx:133-153) only sets activeTabId to filtered[filtered.length-1].id (the LAST tab, not the closed tab's neighbor) and performs no navigation; no other component navigates on activeTabId change (grep across src/renderer). Result: closing the active tab leaves the router on /conversation/<closedId> — the closed conversation stays on screen while the tab bar highlights a different (last) tab; worse, pages/conversation/index.tsx:58-62 re-calls openTab(data) on the next SWR revalidation of the still-mounted closed conversation, re-adding the closed tab. PASTE UNDO: src/renderer/hooks/file/usePasteService.ts:50-54 calls event.preventDefault() for handled plain-text pastes, and src/renderer/components/chat/sendbox.tsx:976-994 onTextPaste inserts the text by computing newValue and calling setInput(newValue) (fallback :993 setInput(text) even REPLACES the whole content). Because the native insertText is prevented and the value is set programmatically via React state, the textarea's native undo stack never records the paste — Ctrl+Z after paste does nothing.
fixSpec: TWO SMALL FIXES. (A) Tab close: in ConversationTabsContext.closeTab (:133-153) select the ADJACENT tab instead of the last: const idx = prev.findIndex(t => t.id === conversationId); newActive = filtered[Math.min(idx, filtered.length-1)] (right neighbor, else left). In ConversationTabs.handleCloseTab (:179-190) compute the same successor from openTabs/activeTabId BEFORE calling closeTab and navigate(`/conversation/${successorId}`) whenever the closed tab was the active one (keep the existing navigate('/guid') for the last tab). Keep the two computations in one exported helper (e.g. nextActiveTabId(tabs, closingId)) so context state and navigation cannot disagree. Also verify closeTabsToLeft/Right/Other paths still navigate correctly when they remove the active tab (they set activeTabId at :175-176/:196-197 but their ConversationTabs callers at :334-344 already navigate — confirm each). (B) Paste undo: in sendbox.tsx onTextPaste (:976-994), stop inserting via setInput. Preferred seam: keep the interception (files must still be intercepted) but insert the cleaned text with document.execCommand('insertText', false, cleanedText) on the focused textarea — execCommand participates in Chromium's native undo stack and fires an input event so React state syncs through the existing onChange; delete the setTimeout caret hack and the whole-content-replacing fallback. Alternative (simpler but loses trailing-newline trim): make PasteService.handlePaste return false for plain text when the event target is the textarea itself, letting the browser paste natively (mirror of the shouldAllowNativePaste logic at PasteService.ts:148-172 that the component-level onPaste path currently bypasses). Do NOT touch the file-paste branch. Check GuidInputCard/useGuidInput (src/renderer/pages/guid/hooks/useGuidInput.ts:95) which shares usePasteService — apply the same insertion fix if it also intercepts text.
testPlan: (A) DOM test with ConversationTabsProvider + a mocked useNavigate: open tabs A,B,C. Case 2 — close an INACTIVE tab: assert navigate NOT called and activeTabId unchanged (kills an over-eager fix that always navigates). Case 3 — close the only tab: navigate('/guid'). title: Uninstaller leaves HKCU residue: darhai:// protocol handler + start-on-boot Run/StartupApproved entries survive uninstall
evidence: resources/windows-installer-x64.nsh and -arm64.nsh contain ONLY the arch-check .onVerifyInstDir function - no customUnInstall macro, no DeleteRegKey/DeleteRegValue anywhere under resources/ (grep confirms). The runtime writes both residues: src/index.ts:1081-1088 calls app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient for PROTOCOL_SCHEMES=['darhai'] (src/process/utils/deepLink.ts:11-14) on every launch -> HKCU\Software\Classes\darhai; src/process/bridge/desktop/applicationBridge.ts:147-155 calls app.setLoginItemSettings -> HKCU\...\CurrentVersion\Run (+ StartupApproved disabled marker); no setAppUserModelId call exists anywhere in src or electron-builder.yml, so Electron's default 'electron.app.Darhai' name applies (package.json name and productName are both 'Darhai'). The .nsh files ARE wired into the installer via scripts/build-with-builder.js:511-521 (--config.nsis.include), so extending them is effective. Fork installs perMachine:true (electron-builder.yml:236), so upstream's documented multi-user HKCU limitation applies with certainty here (elevated uninstall reaches only the admin's hive).
fixSpec: Append a customUnInstall macro to BOTH resources/windows-installer-x64.nsh and windows-installer-arm64.nsh (identical bodies - the build picks one per arch via build-with-builder.js:511-521, so both must stay in sync). Body, adapted from upstream with fork values: gate everything in ${IfNot} ${isUpdated} ... ${EndIf} (electron-builder reruns the OLD uninstaller in update mode on every update; an ungated delete silently kills autostart each update with no self-heal - the fork's setLoginItemSettings only re-runs from the Settings toggle), then DeleteRegKey HKCU 'Software\Classes\darhai' (NOT 'wayland' - fork scheme differs) and DeleteRegValue HKCU 'Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run' 'electron.app.Darhai' plus DeleteRegValue HKCU 'Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\StartupApproved\Run' 'electron.app.Darhai'. Before committing, verify the actual Run value name on a packaged build (install, enable autostart in Settings, inspect HKCU\...\Run) - the 'electron.app.<Name>' fallback is Electron-version-dependent and the fork never calls setAppUserModelId; if the observed name differs, use the observed one and document it. Check ${isUpdated}/${IfNot} availability in the electron-builder NSIS template version the fork pins (upstream relied on it; the fork's electron-builder may differ - if absent, guard via the /updated command-line detection the template uses). Port upstream's tests/unit/windowsUninstallRegistryCleanup.test.ts, adapted to fork names.
testPlan: NSIS is not unit-runnable, so pin the .nsh text (upstream's approach): a test that reads both .nsh files and asserts (1) each contains exactly one '!macro customUnInstall'; (2) the macro body contains DeleteRegKey HKCU 'Software\Classes\darhai', and DeleteRegValue lines for both the Run and StartupApproved\Run paths with value name 'electron.app.Darhai'; (3) every removal directive sits inside an ${IfNot} ${isUpdated} block (assert the gate appears before the first Delete* and ${EndIf} after the last); (4) the extracted macro bodies of x64 and arm64 are byte-identical (sync pin). Mutations proving it: deleting the ${IfNot} ${isUpdated} gate fails (3); changing the scheme key to 'wayland' or dropping the StartupApproved line fails (2); editing only one arch file fails (4) - which is exactly the fake-fix a copy-paste to a single file would produce. Manual verify pass on a packaged Windows build: install -> enable autostart + trigger darhai:// once -> uninstall -> assert both registry paths gone; then install old -> update -> assert autostart value SURVIVES the update-mode uninstaller run.
